CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  March 17, 2020 - 11 :40 A.M.
  City Hall Council Chamber

  SPECIAL MEETING

OPENING:  Vice Mayor Hampton called the special meeting to order at 11 :49
  a.m. The pledge of allegiance was led by Councilmember Gordo.

ROLL CALL:  Mayor Terry Tomek (Absent)
 Councilmembers:  Vice Mayor Tyron Hampton
  Councilmember Victor Gordo
  Councilmember John J. Kennedy (Participated telephonically)
  Councilmember Steve Madison (Participated telephonically)
  Councilmember Gene Masuda (Participated telephonically)
  Councilmember Margaret McAustin (Participated telephonically)
  Councilmember Andy Wilson (Participated telephonically)

  Staff:  City Manager Steve Mermell
  City Attorney/City Prosecutor Michele Beal Bagneris
  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

  ORAL UPDATE - RESPONSE TO COVID-19 OUTBREAK -
  CITY MANAGER

  City Manager Mermell presented a PowerPoint presentation on the
  City's actions and objectives during the COVID-19 outbreak, and
  responded to questions. Dr. Ying Ying Goh, MD, Director of Public
  Health, provided world, national, and local data on the COVID-19
  outbreak and responded to questions. Patrick Cahalan, Pasadena
  Unified School District (PUSD), provided information on PUSD's
  actions and objectives to keep students and their families safe from
  COVID-19 outbreak, and discussed school closures, child care
  programs, and student meal programs; and responded to
  questions. Akila Gibbs, Executive Director of Pasadena Senior
  Center, provided information on the changes of services provided
  to seniors to prevent the spread of COVID-19, and responded to
  questions.

  Councilmember Kennedy suggested that staff look into the actions
  taken by Wuhan, China officials as a learning model, and make any
  necessary implementations to prepare for worst case scenarios of
  a COVID-19 outbreak in Pasadena. He also suggested staff
  contact City of Hope representatives to discuss any assistance that
  may be required during the COVID-19 outbreak.

  Councilmember Madison requested that staff determine if there is
  a shortage of blood supply at Huntington Memorial Hospital.

Council Minutes  1  03/17/2020
   Councilmember McAustin spoke in favor of staff working with
  surrounding municipalities and Los Angeles County, to pursue a
  short, aggressive, and intensive stay-at-home order, for
  approximately 14 to 21days.

  Councilmember Wilson expressed concerns with the staff's
  Emergency Operations Committee, which does not include a
  representative from the Huntington Memorial Hospital, and
  encouraged staff to seek out representatives from the hospital, as
  well as PUSD. He also asked staff to put effort into ensuring the
  availability of COVID-19 testing within the community and by City
  partners such as the Huntington Hospital.

  Councilmember Gordo spoke on the importance of working and
  coordinating with surrounding communities including cities that are
  members of the San Gabriel Valley Council of Governments, and
  the need to consider rejoining (SCVCOG). He asked staff to:

  •  Work with PUSD to determine the capacity of providing
  meals to students and the ability to expand the program to
  provide meals to the most vulnerable in the community
  including children, adults, seniors and disabled individuals;
  •  Work with PUSD to identify foster care facilities to ensure
  these facilities have necessary provisions and are following
  all the correct protocols;
  •  Work with Los Angeles County staff to implement a
  moratorium on foster care kids being graduated from the
  foster care system during the COVID-19 crisis;
  •  Provide information on the authority to declare all City
  employees disaster service workers; and
  •  Consider how staff can be redirected to begin cleaning
  public areas (i.e. train stations, bus stops, public
  restrooms).

  Felicia Williams, Pasadena resident, expressed concerns with
  the COVID-19, specifically the impacts to small businesses;
  asked staff to involve small businesses by having them provide
  meals to those in need using City funds to pay small
  businesses; and spoke on the need to address emotional
  impacts of the outbreak.

  Following discussion, by consensus of the City Council, and on
  order of the Vice Mayor, the information was received and filed.

Council Minutes  2  03/17/2020
   ACTION ITEM: ADOPTION OF A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL RATIFYING THE CITY MANAGER'S DECLARATION
  OF LOCAL EMERGENCY IN RESPONSE TO COVID-19
  PANDEMIC
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  1. Find that the proposed action is exempt from the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to state CEQA Guidelines
  Section 15061 (b)(3) (Common Sense Exemption);
  2. Adopt a resolution ratifying the March 16, 2020, City Manager
  declaration of a local emergency in response to COVID-19; and
  3. Ratify THE DECLARATION OF LOCAL EMERGENCY -
  CORONAVIRUS (COVID-19), AND FIRST SUPPLEMENT TO THE
  DECLARATION OF LOCAL EMERGENCY-CORONAVIRUS (COVID-
  19) instituted by the City Manager to protect members of the public and
  City workers from an undue risk of contracting COVID-19 virus, and
  related actions. (Resolution No. 9769)

  City Manager Mermell responded to questions related to the
  distinction of actions between the City's Local Public Health
  Emergency and the staff recommendation; and stated that staff is
  taking every action necessary and possible for the City to claim
  federal reimbursement for expenses related to the COVID-19
  pandemic.

  Councilmember Gordo requested that the proposed action of the
  City include required language and follow all necessary steps in
  order to ensure that local businesses will be able to qualify for loan
  modifications/assistance under the new Small Business
  Administration (SBA) guidelines.

  In response to Councilmember Gordo's inquiry related to SBA
  guidelines, City Attorney/City Prosecutor Michele Beal Bagneris
  stated that she is not aware of any SBA loan modifications,
  however, the proposed resolution includes specific language that
  refers to the California Disaster Assistance Act.
  Motion:
  Following discussion, it was moved by Councilmember Kennedy,
  seconded by Councilmember Madison, to approve the staff
  recommendation, amended to include direction to the City
  Manager and City Attorney to conform City actions to be applicable
  to Federal and Sate requirements, ensuring City access to
  emergency funding, including funding to assist small businesses:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Gordo, Kennedy, Madison, Masuda,
  McAustin, Wilson, Vice Mayor Hampton,
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Mayor Tomek
  ABSTAIN: None

  Councilmember McAustin asked staff to consider, evaluate and
  prepare a stay-at-home order to be effective as soon as possible,

Council Minutes  3  03/17/2020
   which would effectively require people to stay at home, only
  allowed to leave for essential services, modeled after the San
  Francisco stay-at-home mandate, as she believes this action is the
  most effective in stopping the virus from spreading.

  Councilmembers Madison, Kennedy, and Gordo expressed
  concerns with prematurely moving forward with a stay-at-home
  order that may have unintended consequences related to the
  economic well-being of the community, with Councilmember Gordo
  advocating for a regional approach. Councilmember Gordo asked
  staff to contact representatives from the County of Los Angeles and
  the San Gabriel Valley Council of Governments to determine if a
  regional plan is being developed.

  Councilmember Wilson and Vice Mayor Hampton spoke in support
  of staff preparing a stay-at-home order and to be proactive and
  prepared.

  City Manager Mermell spoke on the City's plans to work with Los
  Angeles County and other surrounding cities to reach a consensus
  on a regional stay-at-home order.

  Councilmember Madison stated the following for the record, 'The
  fact that I don't support the motion [or suggestion] does not mean
  I'm simply hoping that this will go away. What I understand, is the
  City Manager doesn't need any help from us at this particular
  moment in terms of being prepared to respond [quickly] with
  whatever steps are necessary including the kind of curfew that is
  being discussed."

  Councilmember Wilson asked staff to work collaboratively with
  local healthcare providers to rapidly and radically deploy broad-
  based drive-thru testing and to build significate hospital surge
  capacity in our community, including the allocation of staff time and
  City funds.

  ACTION ITEM: CONSIDERATION OF ACTION TO REDUCE
  THE IMPACTS ON RESIDENTS AND LOCAL BUSINESSES
  RELATED TO THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  1.  Find that the proposed action is exempt from the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to state CEQA
  Guidelines Section 15061(b)(3) (Common Sense Exemption); and
  2.  Consider and provide direction on various options to reduce
  the financial burden on residents and local businesses during the
  period of Local Emergency related to the COVID-19 Pandemic.

  City Manager Mermell reported that he spoke with local business
  representatives related to City action to prevent the spread of
  COVID-19 during the current pandemic, and summarized the

Council Minutes  4  03/17/2020
   agenda report related to staff's recommended mitigation actions;
  and responded to questions. Michele Beal Bagneris, City
  Attorney/City Prosecutor, responded to questions related to the
  City's ability to provide fair relief to small businesses in the City.
  Matt Hawkesworth, Director of Finance, responded to questions
  related to the City's action to save money, market liquidity, and
  public debt. Laura Cornejo, Director of Transportation, and Jon
  Hamblen, Parking Manager, responded to questions related to
  impacts of relaxing overnight street parking.

  Florence Annang and Julieta Aragor, Pasadena residents,
  spoke in opposition to employers in the City postponing the
  minimum wage increase scheduled for July 1, 2020.

  Kate Spear, representing UNITE HERE! Local 11, asked that
  the City take steps to protect workers by including just cause
  provisions for terminations as part of the City's emergency
  legislation in order to protect hospitality workers.

  City Clerk Jomsky reported that staff received 11 letters of
  correspondence providing comments on the item, which were
  distributed to the City Council and posted online.

  Councilmember Wilson asked staff to provide additional analysis
  on business tax revenue projections by business type and size.

  Councilmember Gordo requested that staff redeploy career
  services workers to assist residents who are having to apply for
  unemployment benefits. He spoke on the need to provide relief to
  small business owners, suggested that staff explore the possibility
  of the City utilizing reserves to issue loans to small businesses,
  provide assistance by temporarily reduce or halt the collection of
  utility fees, license fees, and health inspection fees. In addition,
  Mr. Gordo requested that staff provide data on the number of
  businesses that have been directly impacted by COVID-19.
  Councilmember Gordo asked staff to consider partnering with non-
  profit organizations to begin meal programs for senior citizens,
  setting aside money from the City's emergency reserves to fund
  such a program for the next 30 to 60 days for those seniors that
  are unable to leave their homes, go shopping, or prepare their own
  meals.

  Councilmember Kennedy, asked staff to work with Vallarta
  Supermarket in Pasadena, as a possible contractor or consultant,
  to provide food services or food preparation, and advocated for the
  City to conduct food distribution through the Jackie Robinson
  Community Center. He spoke in favor of staff assisting small
  business owners to access Small Business Administration (SBA)
  very low interest rate loans, Federal Emergency Management
  Agency (FEMA) grants, and other entities in the federal

Council Minutes  5  03/17/2020
   government, prior to considering the utilization of critical general
  fund dollars to outside entities. He also spoke on the need to
  provide disinfectants and food to the disabled, physically
  challenged, and boarding care facilities. Councilmember Kennedy
  spoke in favor of the City Council authorizing the City Manager to
  spend up to $150,000 to work with vendors who have been
  prequalified by the City's Health Department to provide meals,
  specifically for the elderly, disabled, and other individuals the City
  Council determines are in need.

  Councilmember McAustin asked staff to amend Recommended
  Action C of the staff report to include relaxing overnight parking
  restrictions on a citywide basis; as well as easing parking
  restrictions in both major and smaller business district areas, but to
  ensure not to make any changes to the current regulations related
  to preferential parking for residents. She spoke in support of
  Councilmembers Kennedy's request for City staff to assist small
  business owners and help them access SBA and FEMA loans.
  She also spoke in favor of providing financial assistance to
  organizations (i.e. community kitchens, restaurants) to work
  together with non-profit organizations to provide meals to seniors
  and individuals who are home-bound; and for staff to suspend the
  collection of the City's Underground Utility Surtax, and asked staff
  to agendize a discussion on the item at a future meeting.

  Councilmember Madison expressed concerns with the City Council
  establishing complex economic policies without giving staff an
  opportunity to carefully consider the recommended policy changes.
  He spoke in favor of adopting UNITE HERE! Local 11 's proposed
  ordinance to help minimum wage and low income workers who
  may be laid off; and providing emergency loans to small
  businesses.

  Councilmember Masuda spoke in favor of the staff
  recommendation, the suspension of City's Underground Surtax,
  contacting grocery markets requesting special operating hours for
  seniors, and providing meals for seniors and for those individuals
  with special needs.

  Vice Mayor Hampton asked staff to contact local groceries to
  provide an hour of "Senior Shopping" only. He spoke in favor of
  relaxing overnight restriction parking throughout the City and
  advocated for rental assistance for residents who are unable to pay
  their rent.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Councilmember Gordo,
  Motion:  seconded by Vice Mayor Hampton, to approve the staff
  recommendation Nos. 1 and 2:

Council Minutes  6  03/17/2020
   AYES:  Councilmembers Gordo, Kennedy, Madison, Masuda,
  McAustin, Wilson, Vice Mayor Hampton,
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Mayor Tomek
  ABSTAIN: None

  Councilmember Wilson spoke on the need to take action to prepare
  for an economic recession caused by COVID-19, asking staff to
  consider long-term repercussions, and allocate the City's
  resources in a responsible manner.

  City Manager Mermell stated that once the City Council has
  allocated funds to provide meals for seniors and individuals in
  need, staff will provide information on costs associated with
  providing such meals on a weekly and monthly basis, and report to
  the City Council as soon as possible.

Original Motion:  Following discussion, it was moved by Vice Mayor Hampton,
  seconded by Councilmember Gordo, to authorize the City Manager
  to expend up to $250,000 to provide meals to vulnerable
  individuals, such as, seniors, disabled and others in need, and
  keep the City Council closely appraised of food-insecurity issues.

Substitute Motion:  Following further discussion, it was moved by Councilmember
  Kennedy, seconded by Councilmember McAustin, to authorize the
  City Manager to expend up to $150,000 to provide meals to
  vulnerable individuals, such as seniors, disabled, and other
  Pasadena residents in need, and keep the City closely appraised
  of food-insecurity issues.

  Councilmember Gordo requested that the substitute motion be
  amended to include the appropriation of $150,000, but also provide
  the City Manager with authority to expend up to an additional
  $100,000 for meals for the City's vulnerable population, at his
  discretion, but require that such authority include the consent of the
  City Attorney. (The friendly amendment was not accepted)

Motion:  Following discussion, it was moved by Councilmember Madison,
  seconded by Councilmember Gordo to table the substitute motion:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Gordo, Madison, Masuda, Vice
  Mayor Hampton,
  NOES:  Councilmembers Kennedy, McAustin, Wilson
  ABSENT: Mayor Tomek
  ABSTAIN: None
  (MOTION FAILED)

Council Minutes  7  03/17/2020
 Revised Substitute Motion:  Following further discussion, it was moved by Councilmember
  Kennedy, seconded by Councilmember McAustin, to authorize the
  City Manager to expend up to $150,000 to provide meals to the
  most vulnerable individuals in the City, with the understanding that
  the City Manager return as soon as necessary with further analysis
  on the need for additional funding:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Gordo, Kennedy, Madison, Masuda,
  McAustin, Wilson, Vice Mayor Hampton
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Mayor Tornek
  ABSTAIN: None

  ADOPT A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL ENACTING A
  MORATORIUM ON EVICTION FOR NON-PAYMENT OF RENT
  BY TENANTS IMPACTED BY THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC AND
  CONDUCT  FIRST  READING  OF  "AN  UNCODIFIED
  ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  PASADENA ENACTING A MORATORIUM ON EVICTION FOR
  NON-PAYMENT OF RENT BY TENANTS IMPACTED BY THE
  COVID-19 PANDEMIC"
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  1.  Find that the recommended action is exempt from the
  California Environmental Quality Act ("CEQA") pursuant to State
  CEQA Guidelines Section 15061 (b)(3), the General Rule that
  CEQA only applies to projects that may have an effect on the
  environment;
  2.  Adopt a resolution of the City Council relating to a moratorium
  on eviction for non-payment of rent by residential tenants impacted
  by the COVID-19 Pandemic; and (Resolution No. 9770)
  3.  Conduct first reading of "AN UNCODIFIED ORDINANCE OF
  THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF PASADENA ENACTING
  A MORATORIUM ON EVICTION FOR NON-PAYMENT OF RENT
  BY RESIDENTIAL TENANTS IMPACTED BY THE COVID-19
  PANDEMIC"

  City Manager Mermell summarized the staff report as apart of the
  oral presentation on the item and responded to questions. Michele
  Beal Bagneris, City Attorney/City Prosecutor and Javan Rad, Chief
  Assistant City Attorney, provided information related to
  moratoriums on eviction for non-payment income restrictions, the
  residential and commercial requirements of providing proof of
  financial impacts; and responded to questions. Bill Huang, Director
  of Housing, provided information on Measure H and State
  homeless funds and allocations; and responded to questions.

  City Clerk Jomsky reported that 76 letters in support and 3 letters
  in opposition of the staff recommendation were received by the City
  Clerk's Office, which were distributed to the City Council, posted
  online, and made part of the public record.

Council Minutes  8  03/17/2020
   The following individuals spoke in favor of a moratorium on eviction
  for non-payment of rent, and/or provided comments related to the
  staff recommendation:

  Charles Xu, Pasadena resident
  Allison Henry, representing Pasadena Tenants Union
  Juliana Serrano, Pasadena resident
  Pablo Alvarado, Pasadena resident

  The following individuals expressed concerns, and/or provided
  comments related to the staff recommendation:

  Todd Hays, Pasadena resident
  Adam Bray-Aly, Business owner

  Councilmember Wilson asked staff to consider applying income
  restrictions to the moratorium on eviction for non-payment of rent
  by residential tenants impacted by the COVID-19 Pandemic.

  Councilmember McAustin  spoke  in  favor  of  the  staff
  recommendation.

  Councilmember Madison expressed concerns with the
  documentation requirements that residential tenants must provide
  to support the claim of lost income, which may potentially provide
  a landlord too much discretion to simply reject a tenant's claim.

  In response to Council Madison's request, Javan Rad, Chief
  Assistant City Attorney, stated that staff will amend the Resolution,
  Exhibit A, Page 2, Section 2A to read as follows: "For residential
  properties, no landlord shall endeavor to evict a tenant in either of
  the following situations: ( 1) for non-payment of rent if the tenant
  demanstrates that the tenant is unable to pay rent due to financial
  impacts related to COVID-19 or. .. "

  Javan Rad, Chief Assistant City Attorney stated that the City
  Council is requested to direct the City Manager to sign the
  "Emergency Declarations."

  Councilmember Masuda  spoke  in  favor  of  the  staff
  recommendation.

  Councilmember Kennedy spoke on the need to be fair to tenants
  and landlords; and spoke in favor of the staff recommendation.

  Councilmember Gordo requested that staff ensure that the
  homeless preventions funds are being used for that purpose.

Council Minutes  9  03/17/2020
   Following discussion, it was moved by Councilmember Madison to
  approve the staff recommendation, including the amendment to
  Motion:  Exhibit A, Page 2, Item 2A as detailed above. (MOTION FAILED
  DUE TO LACK OF SECOND)

  Following further discussion, Michele Beal Bagneris, Attorney/City
  Prosecutor,  advised  that  the  recommendation  from
  Councilmember Madison to amend the verbiage to be consistent
  with both the tenant and landlord standards.

  Councilmember Gordo requested that staff immediately notify
  interested parties, including Pasadena-Foothills Association of
  Realtors, tenant rights groups, and tenant unions, that there may
Councilmember Wilson  be homeless prevention dollars for their rental tenants. He also
was excused and left  asked that small property owners be notified providing details on
the meeting at 5:16 p.m.  the process to request relief funds for their tenants who are unable
  to pay their rent. Councilmember Gordo asked staff to consider if
  the City should prefund homeless prevention dollars in the event
  the City Council needs to take action.

  Vice Mayor Hampton requested that staff send a letter to all tenants
  in the City to inform them of the City's homeless prevention funds.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Vice Mayor Hampton,
  Motion  Seconded by Councilmember Gordo, to direct the City Manager to
  execute the Second Supplement to Declaration of Local
  Emergency:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Gordo, Kennedy, Madison, Masuda,
  McAustin, Vice Mayor Hampton
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Councilmember Wilson, Mayor Tomek
  ABSTAIN: None

  Motion  It was moved by Councilmember Kennedy, Seconded by
  Councilmember Masuda, to approve the staff recommendation,
  amended to incorporate the changes to the Resolution, Exhibit A,
  Page 2, Item 2A, as detailed above:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Gordo, Kennedy, Madison, Masuda,
  McAustin, Vice Mayor Hampton
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Councilmember Wilson, Mayor Tomek
  ABSTAIN: None

  "AN UNCODIFIED ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF
  THE CITY OF PASADENA ENACTING A MORATORIUM ON
  EVICTION FOR NON-PAYMENT OF RENT BY RESIDENTIAL
  TENANTS IMPACTED BY THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC"

Council Minutes  10  03/17/2020
   The above ordinance was offered for first reading by Vice Mayor
  Hampton, amended to include the following changes to the
  Ordinance, Page 4, Section 4A, as follows: "For residential
  properties, no landlord shall endeavor to evict a tenant in either of
  the following situations: (1) for non-payment of rent if the tenant
  demonstrates that the tenant is unable to pay rent due to financial
  impacts related to COVID-19 or ... ":

  AYES:  Councilmembers Gordo, Kennedy, Madison, Masuda,
  McAustin, Vice Mayor Hampton
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Councilmember Wilson, Mayor Tomek
  ABSTAIN: None

  Councilmember McAustin, and Vice Mayor Hampton expressed
  appreciation to City Manager Steve Mermell and staff for their work
  to address the COVID-19 Pandemic.

  In response to Councilmember Madison's request related to a
  clerical error, Michele Beal Bagneris, Attorney/City Prosecutor,
  stated that staff would correct the scrivener's error on Page 2, first
  sentence, and replace "regular meeting" with "special meeting" as
  part of the approved resolution.

ADJOURNMENT  On order of Vice Mayor Hampton, the special meeting of the City
  Council adjourned at 5:27 p.m.

  /s/ Terry Tornek
  Terry Tomek, Mayor
  City of Pasadena
